summary: Set or clear a single bit in a per-row bitmap. Bit index a5 selects the bit; the sentinel a5==255 makes the call a no-op returning a1 unchanged. Otherwise computes the row base v6 = 13*a4 + a1 + 1, reads the current byte at v6 + a5/8, writes v7|v8 (set) when a3 is nonzero or ~v7&v8 (clear) when a3 is zero, and returns a5/8. a2 is never read. The 13-byte row stride matches the sibling routines sub_4B4800 and sub_4B4840, which treat the same object with per-row bitmaps.

Compute row base v6 = 13*a4 + a1 + 1, the byte address of the bitmap row for entry a4.
Derive byte index a5/8 and bit mask v7 = 1 << (a5%8) from the bit index a5.
Read the current byte v8 at v6 + a5/8 before modifying it.
a3 selects the operation: nonzero means set the bit, zero means clear it.
When a3 is nonzero, write v7|v8 at v6 + a5/8, setting the selected bit.
When a3 is zero, write ~v7 & v8 at v6 + a5/8, clearing the selected bit.
Return a5/8 on the set/clear path, or a1 on the a5==255 path.
